text: For every subspace W of a finite-dimensional inner product space V, one has V = W ⊕ W⊥.
explanation: Every v splits uniquely as proj_W(v) + (v − proj_W(v)) with the second piece in W⊥, and W ∩ W⊥ = {0} by positive definiteness. This orthogonal decomposition is what makes orthogonal projection — and least squares — work.
